description.value: First Nations-operated campground in the Ashnola Valley, 8.5 km up a gravel road from Highway 3 near Keremeos, with 55 sites on 33 acres, indoor showers, and easy access to the Similkameen River for floating, paddling, and fishing; open May to September.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms the campground's operator (Lower Similkameen Indian Band), address (1400 Ashnola Road, Keremeos BC V0X 1N1 — matching OSM), and key amenities including indoor showers, an arbour, and a cook house per the About page. Reservations are explicitly confirmed ('We do take reservations for campsites'). However, the most recent blog post is August 2019 and all website activity appears to have ceased around that date, making current operating status uncertain; OSM looks_closed=false and seasonal May–Sep tags are the only more-recent signals.
concerns: Website content is outdated — most recent blog post is August 2019 and no activity is visible after that date; current operating status cannot be confirmed from the website alone.

Multiple inconsistent phone numbers appear across the website: sidebar and About page list 1-250-499-1217 (matches OSM), About page also lists (250) 499-5528, and Contact page lists (250) 488-4198 — it is unclear which number is currently active.
Email address is spelled differently on the About page (ebuchstein@smaelqmix.ca) versus the Contact page (ebuchstein@smelqmix.ca) — one is likely a typo; neither can be confirmed as current.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate, First Nations-operated campground with confirmed facilities (55 sites, indoor showers, covered cook house and arbour) on the Highway 3 corridor near Keremeos — a clear benefit to touring cyclists; outdated website warrants a phone verification before publishing but does not disqualify the listing.
